title: Star trails at Paranal
caption: Star trails over the desert near Paranal Observatory, Chile
celestial: Photograph taken at Paranal Observatory, Chile

recognition.text: Published in the ESO image archive. No published rating.

story: Stars leave long, curving paths across the sky in this view from the desert around ESO's Paranal Observatory in Chile. These star trails all seem to circle around a single fixed point, the Earth's Celestial South Pole, seen just above a rust-tinted horizon.

The stars are not really travelling around that point. The effect is caused by the Earth's rotation. As our planet spins, the sky appears to turn around us, and a camera gathering light over a long time records each star as a curved streak rather than a dot.

The point at the centre of the circles is where the Earth's axis points into the southern sky. Stars close to it trace small circles, while those farther away sweep out wider arcs. Photographs like this turn that everyday motion, too slow to notice by eye, into a pattern anyone can see at a glance.

understand.summary: This is a landscape photograph taken near ESO's Paranal Observatory, in visible light. The camera settings and colour processing are not published.
understand.eye: The eye sees stars as fixed points at any one moment; only a long exposure turns the Earth's rotation into visible trails.
